location.heading: M03-L01 · Recognise what a sign asks
location.exact_quote: Start with purpose, then read the specific symbol and any supplementary panel. The official catalogue groups signs by function. Do not rely on colour alone: similar shapes can communicate different duties, and some important signs have distinctive shapes. [Transportstyrelsen: sign catalogue][signs]

location.heading: M03-L01 · Recognise what a sign asks
location.exact_quote: **Requirements.** B1 means yield to vehicles on the crossing road or route. Make that intention clear early and proceed only without danger or obstruction. B2 requires a stop before entering the crossing road or track area. Stop at the stop line; without one, stop immediately before the signal or before entering the crossing road or track area, as applicable. A rolling pause does not meet a stop duty. [Road Signs Regulation, B1–B2][sign-law] · [Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§5 and 19][traffic-law]

location.heading: M03-L01 · Recognise what a sign asks
location.exact_quote: **Worked decision.** You see a warning sign for a narrow section. You reduce speed and look for oncoming traffic before reaching it. You then read any priority instruction at the narrow point. The warning alone did not decide who should pass first.

location.heading: M03-L02 · Combine the instructions
location.exact_quote: **Requirements.** Follow the traffic instructions that apply to you. Where an instruction differs from a general traffic rule, the instruction governs. A steady traffic-light indication takes precedence over a yield or stop sign; a police officer's direction takes precedence over the rules and ordinary traffic instructions. This is not a rule that a green signal cancels every other restriction. Authorised guards also give traffic directions that must be followed. [Traffic Regulation, chapter 2 §§2–4][traffic-law]

location.heading: M03-L02 · Combine the instructions
location.exact_quote: For ordinary vehicle signals: red means stop; red and amber together still mean stop, with green approaching. Green permits movement, subject to other duties and space ahead. Amber means stop unless, when green changes to amber, you are already so close that stopping would be dangerous. Flashing amber requires particular caution; read the signs and applicable rules. Arrow signals apply to the direction indicated. [Road Signs Regulation, chapter 3 §§3–6][sign-law]

location.heading: M03-L02 · Combine the instructions
location.exact_quote: A red lane-control cross closes the lane; a green downward arrow allows its use; a diagonal amber arrow tells you to move in the indicated direction. Make any lane change safely. Signals for pedestrians or public transport are not automatically instructions for your car. [Road Signs Regulation, chapter 3 §§7–15][sign-law]

location.heading: M03-L02 · Combine the instructions
location.exact_quote: **Markings.** A broken centre or lane line identifies a boundary; it does not promise that overtaking is safe. A warning line indicates that crossing is unsuitable because of conditions and may precede a continuous line. Continuous lines and hatched areas have crossing restrictions, with specified exceptions such as a necessary passage around an obstruction under particular caution. A painted line is not an invitation to improvise an exception. [Road Signs Regulation, chapter 4, M1/M3/M8/M9][sign-law] · [Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§9–11][traffic-law]

location.heading: M03-L03 · Find your way without rushing

contextual_diagram_briefs.title: Stopping distances and bus-stop extent

location.heading: M05-L03 · Choose a lawful place to stop
location.exact_quote: **Core requirements.** Do not stop or park where you create danger, unnecessarily obstruct traffic or hide a sign or signal. Normally use the right side in your direction of travel; one-way roads and specified rail-track situations have exceptions. Secure the vehicle against rolling and prevent unauthorised use. Open doors only without danger or unnecessary inconvenience. [Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§47, 50 and 52][traffic-law]

contextual_diagram_briefs.title: Lane changes and joining

location.heading: M04-L02 · Turn with a complete picture
location.exact_quote: For a lane change or significant sideways movement, signal clearly and in time, then check that the movement can be made without danger or unnecessary obstruction. The indicator announces an intention, not a claim on a gap. Drivers who notice another vehicle intending to join their lane must adjust speed to help; when two lanes merge into one, both drivers must adapt with mutual consideration. These duties work together. [Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§43–44 and 65–66][traffic-law]

contextual_diagram_briefs.title: Roundabout entry, path and exit

location.heading: M04-L04 · Choose a safe path through a roundabout
location.exact_quote: **Requirements.** Travel anticlockwise and yield on entry to vehicles already circulating. Choose an appropriate lane for the onward route and obey signs and markings. There is no general requirement to signal solely for entering; signal lane changes and significant sideways movements, and signal right when leaving. Any lane change must be safe and must not create unnecessary obstruction. [Transportstyrelsen: roundabout guide][roundabout] · [Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§13, 22, 43 and 65–66][traffic-law]

contextual_diagram_briefs.title: Parking movement and observation

location.heading: M05-L04 · Manoeuvre where people may appear
location.exact_quote: **Learning approach.** Select a place that offers both a safe entry and a safe departure. Check the full route of the vehicle: front corners can move sideways while you watch behind. Revisit both sides and the path ahead as the manoeuvre develops. contextual_diagram_briefs.title: Emergency bay and escape-route recognition

location.heading: M10-L01 · When the car cannot continue
location.exact_quote: **Tunnel advice is different.** Use hazard lights, move towards the edge or an emergency bay if possible and switch off the engine. For a non-urgent incident, Trafikverket advises staying in the car or protected from traffic close to it while calling for assistance. In an urgent situation, leave for the nearest emergency exit and use the assistance point, emergency phone or 112. In a fire, leave and reach an emergency exit; follow signs, announcements and emergency personnel. Do not turn a non-urgent-tunnel recommendation into advice to stay beside a fire.
